questions.stem: In the worst case, how does the running time of `find_index` grow with the length n of `nums`?

options.why: The loop doesn't visit every element; each pass throws away half of what's left.
Θ(n log n) is the cost of sorting. This function assumes `nums` is already sorted.
It can stop on the first comparison, but that's the best case. The worst case keeps halving.
options.origin: misconception: best case taken for worst case

questions.explain: Each pass either returns or moves lo above mid or hi below it, so the range still in play at least halves. A range of n can halve only about log₂ n times before it's empty.
